text:
jess: quick follow-up from the kernel-selection RFC thread — we need to pick an approach for attention kernels in the serving runtime. two paths: Triton custom kernels vs CUDA/CUTLASS hand-tuned kernels. TL;DR: both have tradeoffs; want to collect actions and owners. :thinking:

ryan: brief notes i pulled from benchmarks last week: Triton protos hit ~0.85x peak throughput of the best CUTLASS kernels on A100 for long sequences (8k) but had 2x faster iteration time for new layouts. CUTLASS wins on tight memory/latency by ~15-25% in steady-state.

anika: also saw Triton easier for autoregressive caching changes — less plumbing to expose custom kernels to kv-cache. CUTLASS needs more infra (custom kernel dispatch + workspace mgmt).

kevin: infra implications: CUTLASS path will require us to maintain more device-build CI, plus we need to keep a small matrix of sm/driver combos. Triton buys portability (single repo) but the Triton dependency has hit some internal driver regressions before.

marta: important product constraint: Dedicated customers want predictable p99 under load. If CUTLASS gives us lower p99 on worst-case shapes (very long seq), that leans us there. but we also value quick model onboarding for hosted.

jess: proposed compromise: two-tier plan
  1) short term (q2): default to Triton kernels for new models to speed onboarding + a fallback CUTLASS optimized path for heavy customers or long seq workloads.
  2) medium term (q3-q4): upstream a small kernel-selection API in runtime so routing can pick Triton vs CUTLASS by model/shape/policy.

ryan: agree. concrete action items:
  - run controlled perf matrix for 4 shapes: short(128), med(1024), long(4096), xlong(8192) across gpus: A100/80GB, H100, and 3090 (for DR dev kits). gather latency/throughput/p99 + memory. owner: ryan. due: 2w (1715175623).
  - prototype a lightweight CUTLASS attention kernel with same ABI as our Triton kernel so runtime can swap implementations. owner: anika + kevin. due: 3w (1715780423).
  - add kernel-selection config: model.metadata['kernel_preference'] and runtime flag --kernel-policy={auto,force-triton,force-cutlass}. owner: jess. due: 1w (1715606023).

anika: for the prototype we should aim for functional parity first (same outputs & numerics) with debug hooks. use the small int8/quantized path too. i'll stub tests.

kevin: infra tasks: add CUTLASS build job to GPU CI, container with cuda 12/12.1 matrix, and nightly perf job. owner: kevin + infra-bot. due: 4w (1716385223).

marta: can we also add a rollout SLO: only route X% traffic to CUTLASS per model initially, and auto rollback if error rate or latency regresses. product + runtime can set default 5% canary.

jess: yes, we'll wire that into rollouts. action: jess to open RFC follow-up doc with these items and link PRs.

infra-bot: note: triage ticket created: INF-1247 "kernel-selection perf matrix".

ryan: quick opt question: do we allow mixed kernel per-layer? e.g., use CUTLASS for self-attn at final layers and Triton elsewhere to save memory. seems plausible but complicates scheduling.

anika: mixed per-layer might be a good later optimization. for now keep whole-model kernel choice to reduce complexity. can revisit once selection API is stable.

kevin: one more ops note: we need deterministic fallback semantics on OOMs: runtime should attempt Triton->CUTLASS or vice versa based on policy and signal errors to console.

jess: final checklist to confirm: perf matrix (ryan), CUTLASS prototype (anika), CI infra (kevin), kernel-selection flag & metadata (jess), rollout canary policy (marta). i'll assign owners in the RFC doc. meeting Friday to review results. :white_check_mark:
